title: fix(core): the authz prelude's grant read projects the columns it decides on
body:
Fixes #24896

Clause-②: no (a read's projection: every resolved authz answer is unchanged and pinned so; no accept set, served shape or export moves)

## What changed

The authorization prelude (`resolveUserAuthzGrants` in `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`) read `sys_user_permission_set` with no projection, so the engine computed every formula field of the grant table on every request a grant holder made. That read now names exactly the four columns the resolver decides on, through the module-private `tryFind`, which gains an optional `fields` argument. No new export, no error code, and no other read in the prelude changes.

### The columns, measured before the edit (base `74fcec1edb`)

| column | read by | via |
|---|---|---|
| `permission_set` | `grantSetNameOf` | `anchorReadsDefaultOrganization`, `mayApply`, the ledger names, `anchorsPlatformStanding`, the 6b set loop |
| `organization_id` (helper also accepts `organizationId`) | `grantOrganizationOf` | `grantAppliesInTenant`, `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding`, `mayApply`, `applyingGrants` |
| `valid_from` (also `validFrom`) | `isGrantActive`, `nextGrantValidityBoundary` | the `upsRows` filter; the grants-cache boundary over `upsRowsAll` |
| `valid_until` (also `validUntil`) | `isGrantActive`, `nextGrantValidityBoundary` | same |

Nothing in the prelude reads a grant row's `id`, `user_id` (it is only the filter), `granted_by`, `reason` or `display_title`. The camelCase spellings are not declared fields of the object, so the engine never returns them under those keys; only the declared names are projected.

### What a projection does in objectql

`planFormulaProjection` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`) evaluates only the formula fields a non-empty `fields` list names. A list of stored columns yields an empty plan, so no formula is computed and the hop a formula would read is never issued. (#22300's widening applies only when a formula field is IN the projection.) No system column has to be named: driver-sql answers exactly the named columns, `id` included only when named, and the resolver reads no `id`.

### The counts, on the rig of `auth-prelude-query-count.pin.test.ts` (a principal with one organization-owned direct grant)

| core | `display_title` | reads | round trips |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | as declared (own columns) | 8 | 4 |
| `main` | PR #24885's one-hop formula (applied in the test fixture only) | 9 (`sys_user` 3) | 5 |
| this PR | PR #24885's one-hop formula | 8 | 4 |

## Pins

- **Equivalence** (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.grant-projection.test.ts`, new). Each fixture is resolved twice on the batch-equivalence recording double: over full stored rows plus a computed title, as the unprojected read answered, and over projected rows (named columns only, no `id`), as a driver answers a projection. The whole envelope must be identical. Fixtures: an active grant in the active organization, one owned by another organization, an expired one, one not yet valid, one inside its window, a deployment-wide one (`organization_id` null) with and without an active organization, an `admin_full_access` grant owned by the Default Organization (acting elsewhere, and with none active), an expired `admin_full_access` grant, another organization's `admin_full_access`, and all states at once. The batch-equivalence `FIXTURES` matrix runs through the same comparison. A further case pins that the grant read names exactly the four columns and that no other prelude read names any.
- **Count** (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-prelude-query-count.pin.test.ts`). The rig gains an optional direct grant, and a variant of the grant table whose `display_title` reads one hop through `user_id`, with the same expression as PR #24885. A new grant-holder case runs under both titles and holds 8 reads in 4 round trips. The case first proves the hop is live on that engine: an unprojected read computes `Prelude → prelude_editor` from the user's name.

## Verification (head `41b479266`, after merging `origin/main` at `71696121a`)

- **Ablation:** projection reverted (`--hold` with a dist marker, preflight proved the marker in core's `dist/`). The count pin went red only under the one-hop title (`sys_user` 3, expected 2). The equivalence pin's projection case went red. Restore: `ablation-replace` reports blob == HEAD (`6d3b1baf7150`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Rebuild and `ablation-dist-preflight --absent` report the marker absent from all 14 built files and the tree clean.
- **Column sweep:** each of the four columns dropped from the projection in turn. Envelope-equivalence fixtures went red every time: `permission_set` 11 failed, `organization_id` 11, `valid_from` 3, `valid_until` 6. Every leg restored blob == HEAD.
- **Suites (exit 0 each):**
  - `@objectstack/core` test: 108 files / 2623 tests.
  - `@objectstack/core` `test:repo`: 6 / 82.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-security` test: 196 files / 4075 passed, 45 skipped.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-auth` test: 171 files / 3283 passed, 10 skipped.
- **Typecheck:** `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/plugin-auth` both exit 0. Both test layers compile with no new debt.
- **Build:** the full build (`turbo run build`, docs excluded) exits 0.
- **Gates:** `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 70 families, all run with exit 0, and `--ran` reconciles: 70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, all exit codes recorded. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (no `dist` yet). `check:lean-entry-closure` first exited 1, because it read `spec`'s `dist` while the full build was rewriting it. Both exit 0 when re-run on the finished build.
- **Pin sweep:**
  - The batch-equivalence and request-rounds goldens record `object`, `where`, `limit` and `isSystem`, never `fields`, so none moves.
  - No pin anywhere asserts the grant read's options exactly.
  - The one pin that moves is the query-count pin, which gains its grant-holder case.

## Cross-lane

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-prelude-query-count.pin.test.ts` is in `domain:services`' package. The claim declares this edit as cross-lane, and the seat declares it to that lane before the queue.

## Acceptance notes

- `sys_member` and `sys_user_position`, the prelude's other grant reads, are also unprojected. Each declares an own-column `display_title` formula (`sys_member`: user and role; `sys_user_position`: user and position), so today they cost one CEL evaluation per row and no read. They would carry the same read cost if either title gained a hop. Measured and named only; not built (out of scope per the claim).
- The grants cache default (`OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS=0`) is untouched.
- PR #24885 can merge `main` after this lands: its formula then adds no read or round trip to the prelude.
